misreadings.quote: yet we now see this was an unnecessary sacrifice
misreadings.evidence: "It was not a lot, but it had not been touched in the meantime"; "This money, however, was certainly not enough to enable the family to live off the interest; it was enough to maintain them for, perhaps, one or two years, no more."
misreadings.explanation: The text says the old savings were small and insufficient for the family to live on, and that it was "better the way his father had done things", so calling Gregor's work plainly unnecessary is stated as fact beyond what the text supports.

misreadings.quote: his youth was sold for a surplus they already possessed
misreadings.evidence: "they had not been using up all the money that Gregor had been bringing home every month, keeping only a little for himself, so that that, too, had been accumulating."
misreadings.explanation: Part of the surplus was Gregor's own earnings saved by the family, and the older money was small, so it was not a surplus already in hand before he worked.

result.note: Most of the reflection's claims about the text hold (the father's savings, Gregor's enthusiasm, the fading view, Grete's window ritual, the bedsheet), and the problems are overstatements about the savings, mostly in the prose version.
